sections.title: Form and leaves
sections.text: Swedish whitebeam, traditionally called Sorbus intermedia and treated by Kew as Hedlundia intermedia (also published as Scandosorbus intermedia), is a deciduous tree commonly about 6–12 m tall. Its broad, shallowly lobed leaves have a pale, felted underside, unlike the pinnate leaves of rowan (Sorbus aucuparia).

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Flat clusters of white flowers are followed by red, apple-like fruits about 1.3 cm long. The plate shows the simple, lobed leaves and clustered flowers characteristic of Swedish whitebeam.

sections.title: Use and safety
sections.text: This species is grown as an ornamental and street tree. The sources consulted do not establish a food use for its fruit.
